newsitem.title: FRANCE: S&P lowers Renault Credit Intnl rating to A2.
newsitem.headline: S&P lowers Renault Credit Intnl rating to A2.

text.p: Rating agency Standard & Poor's ADEF said it was lowering the long-term debt rating of Renault Credit International SA Banque to A2 from A1.
Other ratings of Renault and its units were confirmed and removed from the surveillance list.

"The fall in the long-term paper rating primarily reflects the significant drop in the group's profitability due to the deterioration of the car division's competitive position in its home market, seen by the lack of sales growth in a market that rose 14 percent in the first nine months of the year," it said.

It said in a statement that Renault's new policy to cut prices to boost sales would help restore its position in the market but would have a negative impact on margins. Adding to the pressure is a doubtful outlook for the French car market after the end of more than two years of government rebates.
Renault reported a drop in net attributable profit to 158 million francs in the first half of 1996 from 1.76 billion a year earlier and predicted a loss for the year.
However, S&P said, "the group should maintain a solid financial structure despite the expected drop in its cashflow due mainly to a decline in investment outlays".
It left its rating on short-term notes for Renault and some subsidiaries at A-2.
